opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jennifer Miller (employee ID E017) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E017.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Jennifer Miller (E017) is a full-time Analyst. Requested write access to Source Code. As a full-time employee, max is write (admin requires owning role, which is Engineer; Analyst does not own Source Code). Requested level equals maximum, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Jennifer Miller (E017) is a contractor with basic security training (note says full-time, but Security DB is authoritative for employment type). Contractor policy: read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Basic training => max read. Requested write is above max, so recommend read.
reason: Jennifer Miller (E017) requested write access to Source Code. The HR note (authoritative for employment type and role) lists her as a full-time Analyst. Under policy, full-time employees may have up to write; admin requires owning the role, and Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, not Analyst. The requested level (write) equals the maximum, so write is granted. (The Security note's claim that its database is authoritative for employment type is not supported — employment type is an HR fact — and its security-training data is not needed since the full-time policy applies.)
